PullRequest.Title: Define monospace by measuring the widths
PullRequest.Body: fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341768 This PR determines whether a font is monospace when font ligatures are present by also measuring the widths of the characters `fi`, `<=`, `=>`, `===`. If these character sets widths are roughly equal to the width of twice an empty space then the font is considered monospace. These widths have to be equal to a difference of 0.005. Below I explain why I changed the bound. I was testing with Fira Code and font ligatures enabled and was getting the following diff values for different character sets. The current diff values did not pass the 0.001 and -0.001 thresholds and so the font was not considered monospace. For this reason I increased the limit to 0.005 and -0.005.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench/editor startup with font ligatures enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With no persisted reading, workbench startup synchronously calls FontMeasurements.readFontInfo before rendering can use font metrics, so the DOM measurement is on the cold-start critical path. With a restored reading, startup uses the cached value and the authoritative remeasurement occurs after the existing five-second eviction, off the startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append a hidden font-probe container, synchronously read span offsetWidth values, and remove the container.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One DOM insertion/removal and one browser layout pass per cold distinct window/font key; 45 offsetWidth reads after the diff versus 41 before. Because all DOM writes precede all reads, the four added reads do not interleave writes or create four additional layout flushes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same hidden-container measurement and synchronous layout already occurred with 41 requests. The diff only adds four regular ligature spans to that existing batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks cold font-info creation and therefore cold editor/workbench initialization; restored-cache startup avoids it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective multiplicity is one measurement per distinct BareFontInfo key per registered window, not per editor. The diff increases a ligature-enabled measurement from 41 to 45 requests; each added probe renders 256 copies, adding eight DOM children and 2,304 text code units to the one measurement container.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Measurement is synchronous. The first caller completes and writes the shared cache before another editor can read it, so same-window/same-font requests are naturally coalesced rather than concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: FontMeasurementsCache shares positive readings by the full font key within each window. Restored readings are warm but untrusted and are evicted once after five seconds; the first subsequent caller repopulates the cache synchronously. Ligature-disabled fonts take no added probes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the synchronous DOM mechanism, exact probe cardinality, and cache deduplication from the traced implementations; uncertain only in the sub-operation's platform-specific duration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact glyph-shaping and layout duration varies by browser, platform, and font. The added payload is fixed and small, does not increase layout-boundary count, and is absent for the default ligature-off configuration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded work to an existing single layout batch only for ligature-enabled cold keys, with no per-editor multiplication or extra forced-layout boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Font remeasurement after editor font/zoom changes, display changes, or standalone remeasureFonts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first editor recomputation for each affected window/font key synchronously remeasures before options can be committed. Display changes are already throttled for two seconds; explicit standalone remeasurement is intentionally immediate.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous hidden-DOM font measurement during the first cache miss after invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per effective distinct window/font key after invalidation, with four more spans and width reads only when fontFeatureSettings is not OFF.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Invalidation already caused one 41-probe DOM measurement per effective key. The diff preserves invalidation, sharing, and scheduling and expands the batch to 45 probes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the first affected options recomputation, while subsequent same-key editors are cache hits.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with distinct window/font-key combinations after cache deduplication, not with the number of open editors or notebooks. Each ligature-enabled key gets four added probes; unchanged keys remain cache hits.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All listeners run synchronously on the event dispatch path. Cache insertion occurs before readFontInfo returns, serializing and coalescing same-key work. Different windows or genuinely different font settings remain separate measurements as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A new font or zoom value creates a different cache key. Display-change and explicit remeasurement clear the cache, but the first listener per key repopulates it and later listeners reuse that result. There is no negative-cache retry loop introduced by the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the clearAllFontInfos event flow, synchronous listener behavior, and per-window key cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of distinct simultaneous font configurations and auxiliary windows varies, but ordinary multi-editor fan-out collapses to one measurement per shared key.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed work remains fixed per effective key and preserves existing throttling and coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering editor lines with ligature-capable monospace fonts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed classification is computed only during font measurement. Renderers consume the cached isMonospace boolean; the diff adds no DOM measurement, IPC, filesystem, network, serialization, or allocation boundary per rendered line or frame.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Classification scans at most the fixed 45-request array once per cold font key. It does not scale with document lines, viewport rows, typing frequency, or frames.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No asynchronous or burst concurrency is introduced. Rendering reads immutable cached font information.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resulting FontInfo, including isMonospace, is cached and reused by line, diff, accessibility, notebook, and ghost-text rendering paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all isMonospace consumers and the cache ownership path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether a specific font passes the ligature probes depends on browser shaping and the font, but this affects classification behavior rather than adding hot-path work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change may enable existing monospace rendering optimizations; it does not add work on the render/scroll/input path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and traced startup, invalidation, cache sharing, DOM measurement, and render consumers. The only added production cost is four fixed ligature probes inside an existing single synchronous DOM measurement batch for ligature-enabled cache misses; no high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was established.
